claim: The Production front 'Thanks.' is a hair away from 'Thank you.', which I already answer with どうもありがとう or ありがとうございます, so I will say one of those instead of どうも.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Greetings / Thanks.' Earlier cards: chapter-3 どうもありがとう | 'Thank you.'; chapter-0 ありがとうございます | 'Thank you.' The difference between the three is only in this card's note ('A casual, shortened thanks').
fix: Add a hint such as 'short, casual' to the Production front so it cannot be answered with either of the full Thank-you cards.

claim: The English starts with 'Then', which this deck teaches as じゃ, but the target has no じゃ.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Then please give me six of those.' Answer: 'それをむっつください'. Compare chapter-5-extras/ja-sore-o-nihon-kudasai: 'Right, then two bottles of those, please.' -> 'じゃ、それを２ほんください', and chapter-4 じゃ | 'Well then'.
fix: Either drop 'Then' from the English or add じゃ、 to the target.

claim: 'It's from England.' fits イギリスです just as well as イギリスのです; every earlier 'from X' card I know answers with a bare Xです.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'It's from England. / answering where the coffee cup is from'. Answer: 'イギリスのです'. Earlier: chapter-1-extras インドです | 'He's from India.', ちゅうごくです | 'I'm from China.', イギリスです | 'I'm from the United Kingdom.'
fix: Word the English so it asks for the の: 'It's an English one.' (the way iie-doitsu-no-desu says 'No, they're German ones.').

claim: The romaji 'happon' is not split like every other doubled counter in the same series ('ip-pon', 'rop-pon', 'jup-pon').
evidence: counter-hon-8 Says: 'happon'. counter-hon-1 Says: 'ip-pon'; counter-hon-6: 'rop-pon'; counter-hon-10: 'jup-pon'.
fix: Write it 'hap-pon' to match the rest of the ほん series.

claim: The English is spelled 'Cheese cake' as two words, while the same item is 'cheesecakes' on an extras card.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Food / Cheese cake'. chapter-5-extras/chiizukeeki-appurupai-kudasai: 'I would like three cheesecakes and two apple pies, please.'
fix: Spell it 'Cheesecake'.

claim: The note explains あちら as the polite form of あそこ, a word no card has taught me by this lesson, so the explanation leans on nothing I know.
evidence: Note: 'Over there. Polite form of あそこ (asoko); used for a place distant from both speaker and listener.' あそこ does not appear in the ledger or in either Lesson 5 unit (its card is in a much later lesson).
fix: Drop the reference to あそこ here, or gloss it as a new word ('the plain word, あそこ (asoko), comes later').

claim: The note says to use どちら 'from Lesson 1' for a choice between two, but Lesson 1 taught どちら only as the polite word for 'where'.
evidence: Note: 'For a choice between two, use どちら (dochira), from Lesson 1.' chapter-1/dochira: 'Where (polite word for どこ)'. chapter-5/dore's note makes the same 'between two' claim without the back-reference.
fix: Say that どちら has a second use, 'which of two', which is new here, instead of pointing back to a card that taught something else.

claim: This card asks for exactly the same thing as a base card: 'Fifth floor' -> ５かい and '5th floor' -> ごかい are the same word.
evidence: chapter-5-extras/5th-floor Production FRONT: 'Directions / 5th floor', Answer: 'ごかい'. chapter-5/fifth-floor Production FRONT: 'Directions / Fifth floor', Answer: '５かい'.
fix: Keep one of the two cards.

claim: This card asks for exactly the same thing as a base card: 'First floor' -> １かい and '1st floor' -> いっかい are the same word.
evidence: chapter-5-extras/1st-floor Production FRONT: 'Directions / 1st floor', Answer: 'いっかい'. chapter-5/ikkai-sub Production FRONT: 'Directions / First floor', Answer: '１かい'.
fix: Keep one card; the extras one has the useful ground-floor note, so move that note onto whichever survives.

claim: The note's reasoning contradicts the この/その/あの rule this lesson teaches: if the camera is now 'the near one' for the assistant, the assistant should say これ, not それ.
evidence: Answer: 'はい、それもにほんのです'. Note: 'The customer says その (sono) and the assistant answers それ (sore) — from behind the counter the same camera is now the near one.' chapter-5-extras/sono-kamera-wa-amerika-no note: 'その is the thing nearer the person you are talking to.' chapter-5/kono note pairs この with これ.
fix: Make the note and the target agree with the rule: either answer これも, or explain それ as pointing back to the thing just mentioned, not as 'the near one'.

claim: The note says a place before の 'never' says who a thing belongs to, but earlier cards use a place or company before の for exactly that.
evidence: Note: 'A place before の (no) says where the thing was made, never who it belongs to — this bag is not owned by England.' Earlier: chapter-2-extras 'これはかいしゃのでんわです | This is the company phone.'; 'のぞみデパートのでんわばんごうは... | The Nozomi Department Store's telephone number...'; chapter-1 'とうきょうだいがくのラジャです | I am Raja of the University of Tokyo.'
fix: Soften 'never' to something true for this pair, e.g. 'with a country before の, it usually means where it was made'.

claim: The note gives the ほん to ぽん rule as 'after いち, ろく and じゅう', leaving out はち, though the base unit teaches はっぽん.
evidence: Note: 'ほん (hon) hardens to ぽん (pon) after いち (ichi), ろく (roku) and じゅう (jū) — hence いっぽん (ip-pon), ろっぽん (rop-pon), じゅっぽん (jup-pon).' chapter-5/counter-hon-8: 'はっぽん | Eight (long objects)'.
fix: Add はち / はっぽん (hap-pon) to the list.

claim: The note says glasses take つ because they are round, but the base unit teaches つ as the general counter for things with no special counter, not a counter for round things.
evidence: Note: 'Glasses are round so they take つ (tsu), plates are flat so they take まい (mai).' chapter-5/fib-c5-coffee-cup-quantity note: 'つ covers everyday objects like cups when no dedicated counter fits.' The つ cards are glossed 'general objects'.
fix: Say glasses take つ because つ is the general counter, matching the base note.

claim: The note links おくじょう to ちゅうしゃじょう through a shared じょう meaning 'place'; I have never met ちゅうしゃじょう, and the claim reads as doubtful for a word meaning 'rooftop'.
evidence: Note: 'Shares the じょう (jō) 'place' ending with ちゅうしゃじょう (chūshajō).' ちゅうしゃじょう appears on no card in the ledger or in Lesson 5.
fix: Drop the comparison, or replace it with a check that the two じょう really are the same element.

claim: The deck's own yellow card says きいろい and きいろの are equally correct, so 'These are yellow socks.' has two right answers and the front cannot ask for the の form this card exists to teach.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Colors / These are yellow socks.' Answer: 'これはきいろのくつしたです'. chapter-5-extras/yellow note: 'きいろい シャツ (kiiroi shatsu) and きいろの シャツ (kiiro no shatsu) are equally correct.' This card's note: 'The same colour in its の form — both are correct here.'
fix: Add a hint such as 'using the の form' to the Production front.

claim: The mirror case of eg-kiiro-no-kutsushita: 'This is a yellow umbrella.' accepts きいろのかさ too, per the deck's own yellow note, and nothing on the front picks the い form.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Colors / This is a yellow umbrella.' Answer: 'これはきいろいかさです'. Note: 'きいろ (kiiro) is one of only two colours with both forms.'
fix: Add a hint such as 'using the い-adjective form', so the pair of cards each ask for their own form.

claim: 'Where are you from?' is what I would answer with おくにはどちらですか, which I learned in Lesson 1 as 'What country are you from?'
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Nationalities & Countries / Where are you from?' Answer: 'しゅっしんはどこですか？'. chapter-1-extras: 'おくにはどちらですか | What country are you from?'
fix: Add a hint naming the new word or the sense, e.g. 'asking about hometown, with しゅっしん'.

claim: The note cites ジャックさんはフランスじんですか as being 'in this lesson', but that card is in Lesson 1's extras.
evidence: Note: '...like ジャックさんはフランスじんですか (Jakku san wa furansu jin desu ka?) in this lesson.' The ledger lists that sentence under 'Lesson 1: Meeting: Nice to Meet You (Extras)'.
fix: Change 'in this lesson' to 'from Lesson 1'.

claim: 'Where is the hotel address?' is not natural English for asking what an address is, so the Production front reads oddly.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Travel & Tourism / Where is the hotel address?' Answer: 'ホテルのじゅうしょはどこですか'. Earlier: chapter-2-extras 'ホテルのじゅうしょは | The hotel address is'.
fix: Gloss it as 'What is the hotel's address?' and, if the どこ is the point, say so in a note.

claim: 'Where is that wine from?' can be said two ways this chapter teaches, and two other cards with the same English shape use the other one.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Where is that wine from?' Answer: 'そのワインはどこのですか'. chapter-5/fib-c5-coffee-cup-origin-q: 'Where is that coffee cup from?' -> 'それはどこのコーヒーカップですか'; chapter-5-extras/kore-wa-doko-no-biiru-ka: 'Where is this beer from?' -> 'これはどこのビールですか'.
fix: Add a hint naming the shape wanted, e.g. 'starting from そのワイン'.

claim: 'Where is that camera over there from?' could be あれはどこのカメラですか, the shape two other cards with the same English use, as easily as the target.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Where is that camera over there from?' Answer: 'あのカメラはどこのですか'. Same-shape cards: chapter-5/fib-c5-coffee-cup-origin-q -> 'それはどこのコーヒーカップですか'; chapter-5-extras/kore-wa-doko-no-biiru-ka -> 'これはどこのビールですか'.
fix: Add a hint such as 'starting from あのカメラ'.

claim: The note talks about 'Member 3 of the set' and says これ 'becomes' それ, both pointing at sibling cards I never see next to this one.
evidence: Note: 'Member 3 of the set. か (ka) on the end is the whole of the question; the word order does not change. これ (kore) becomes それ (sore) because you are now asking about the other person's side.' itaria-no-kutsu-ja-arimasen has 'Member 2 of the set.' the same way.
fix: Drop the set numbering and say what the note means on its own: 'それ, because the shoes are on the other person's side'.

claim: The note says bottles took ほん 'two lines earlier in the same dialogue', but this is a card authored for the deck and I never see any dialogue.
evidence: Note: 'Bottles took ほん (hon) two lines earlier in the same dialogue.' Card is marked '(authored for the deck, not printed in the book)'.
fix: Replace the dialogue reference with the card it means, e.g. 'compare そのワインを２ほんください'.

claim: Like the coffee-cup answer, 'It's from France.' fits フランスです as well as フランスのです, and the earlier 'from X' cards all answer with a bare Xです.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'It's from France. / answering where the wine is from'. Answer: 'フランスのです'. Earlier: chapter-1-extras ドイツです | 'I'm from Germany.', アメリカです | 'I'm from the United States.'
fix: Gloss it 'It's a French one.' so the の is asked for.
